messages.content:
can you complete this task for yourself? Build a generic batch renderer: the operator points the agent at a job folder of prompts and reference assets, and it renders the whole sequence through MiniMax H3 unattended.

A:\Users\rhine\Documents\Codex\2026-08-07\referenced-chatgpt-conversation-this-is-an-2\COMFYUI_STORY_HANDOFF_2026-08-09

This is not Equal Shares. It must never read or write outputs/equal_shares/** state — no touching audio_pass_manifest.json, story_config.json, or voice_requirements.json. It is a second, general pipeline that happens to reuse the same proven render infrastructure.
Read first
docs/reference/MINIMAX_PROMPT_GUIDE_ref.md §2.1–2.5 and §4.1 — the reference label and marker rules. Quoted below where they matter; verify them.
docs/GOLDEN_REFERENCE/PROVEN_FACTS.md §1 — the settings that must not change
work/render_single_pass.py — build_ref2va_workflow, build_fl2va_workflow, start_comfy, stop_comfy, submit_workflow, wait_for_completion. Reuse these. Do not rewrite the render path.
work/thermal_guard.py, work/duration_ladder.py
THE MOST IMPORTANT THING IN THIS DOCUMENT
Socket numbers are zero-based. Prompt tags are one-based. They are not the same number and confusing them is the single most likely way this ships broken.

Operator's name
ComfyUI socket
Prompt tag
Role
img 0
ref_images.ref_image_0
<Picture 1>
character reference
img 1
ref_images.ref_image_1
<Picture 2>
setting — stays the same
img 2
ref_images.ref_image_2
<Picture 3>
second character, when present
video ref
first video socket
<Video 1>
motion only


Tags follow connection order, so if a slot is empty the later tags shift down. Three images wired means <Picture 1>, <Picture 2>, <Picture 3>. Two images wired means <Picture 1> and <Picture 2> — never <Picture 3>.

This project already has a scar from exactly this class of bug: a prompt declared <Audio 2> while the reference was wired into ref_audio_0, so every voice in the clip was mis-attributed. Four clips were affected. See CHANGELOG/2026-08-18c_one_off_speaker_rule.md.

Also: the operator's existing hand-made renders used <Video 0>. That is non-conforming — the guide is one-based throughout. A tag of <Video 0> likely bound to nothing, which would explain why those prompts needed heavy prose to compensate. Emit <Video 1>.
Job 1 — verify the video socket before building anything
Do not assume MiniMaxH3ReferenceToVideo accepts a video reference. The project's 15 proven-good graphs use image and audio references only; a video reference socket has never been exercised here.

Establish the truth, in this order:

Query the running ComfyUI at /object_info for the node's real input schema
If a video socket exists, record its exact name
If it does not, stop and report that — the motion-reference feature cannot be built on a socket that is not there, and the operator needs to know rather than receive something that silently ignores the video

Write what you find into the CHANGELOG. This is the one genuine unknown.
Job 2 — the job folder layout
The operator points at one folder. Detect this structure:

<job>/

  prompts/       0001.txt, 0002.txt, ...      one per render, sorted

  video_refs/    00.mp4, 01.mp4, ...          motion reference per render

  img0/          character reference

  img1/          setting reference

  img2/          second character (optional)

  renders/       created by you — output goes here

Slot filling rule — auto-detect, do not ask:

a slot folder holding one file → that file is used for every render
a slot folder holding numbered files → matched sequentially to the prompt index

So img1/ with a single setting.png stays fixed across the whole batch, while img0/ with 00.png, 01.png, … advances per render. That covers both cases the operator described without any configuration.

Accept flat layouts too — files named prompt_001.txt, video_001.mp4, img0_001.png in one folder. Sort naturally, so 2 comes before 10.

Report the plan before rendering anything. A dry run that prints, per render: prompt file, video ref, each image slot, resolved tags, duration, output path. The operator must be able to see the whole batch is correctly paired before a single frame is generated. Mismatched counts are reported as a warning with the pairing shown, not silently truncated.
Job 3 — the motion-only lock, done properly
The operator's rule: the video reference supplies motion only. The model must never copy imagery from it.

The guide has a canonical construction for exactly this. From §2.1:

<Subject 1> is the woman whose appearance comes from <Picture 1> and whose

walking motion comes from <Video 1>.

That is the correct way to say it — appearance sourced from the image, motion sourced from the video, in the subject definition where the model expects it.

And retention_analysis gets the matching marker. From §4.1 the visible-content markers are fully_preserved, partially_preserved, attribute_transfer, weak_reference, and the guide's own example for a structural video reference is:

<Video 1> (cut and pacing structure): weak_reference - ...

So emit, for a motion-only video:

<Video 1> (motion and camera structure only): weak_reference - only the movement,

timing, and camera behaviour are taken from <Video 1>. None of its people,

faces, bodies, clothing, setting, or lighting appear in the target video.

Plus the identity line pinning appearance to <Picture 1>.

This is stronger than prose alone because retention_analysis is the section this project already proved the model actually acts on — adding it is what removed the doubled voice after weeks of prose failing to.

Build all three pieces automatically: the subject definition, the retention line, and a short confirming sentence in detailed_description. The operator's prompt files should not have to contain any of it.
Job 4 — the renderer
New work/batch_render_folder.py. Reuse the existing infrastructure; do not reimplement it.

Non-negotiable, from PROVEN_FACTS.md §1:

ref2va      minimax_h3_ref2va_pruned_nvfp4.safetensors

fl2va       minimax_h3_fl2va_pruned_int8_convrot.safetensors

encoder     qwen3vl_32b_minimax_h3_nvfp4_awq.safetensors

VAEs        minimax_h3_video_vae_fp16 + minimax_h3_audio_vae_fp32

sampler     res_multistep / simple, denoise 1.0, 20 steps

fps/depth   24 / 8-bit

frames      congruent to 5 modulo 17

Megapixels is a CLI argument, defaulting to 0.9 for picture work. Turbo checkpoints, nodes and LoRAs stay prohibited.

Operational rules, all reusing what exists:

one backend per render, stopped after, thermal_guard before and after
claim render_queue_owner.json — never run beside the Equal Shares pass
resume: skip renders whose output already exists, unless --force
never overwrite. Attempt N goes to a new file; nothing is replaced
per-job manifest inside the job folder, recording for every render: prompt file, every reference path, resolved tags, seed, duration, frames, megapixels, output path, status
--limit N so the operator can try three before committing to eighty
on VRAM failure, drop 0.1 MP and record it; floor at 0.4 MP for picture

If a prompt has dialogue, reuse duration_ladder.py for retries — same rule, duration not seed. If it has none, a failed render retries once then reports.
Job 5 — validate before spending GPU time
Every assembled prompt goes through local_agent/validate_h3_prompt.py before it is submitted. A prompt that fails is reported with its faults and skipped, not rendered.

Eighty renders at several minutes each is hours. Catching a malformed prompt beforehand costs milliseconds.

Note honestly in the CHANGELOG: that validator was written for this project's six-section dialogue prompts and passes 124/124 of them. Behaviour on motion-reference prompts is unproven — if it produces false positives on valid batch prompts, fix the validator with a recorded measurement, do not disable the check.
Job 6 — expose it to the agent
Two tools in local_agent/tools.py:

batch_plan — {"folder": "..."}. Scans, pairs, resolves tags, validates every prompt, returns the plan. Read-only, renders nothing.
batch_render — proposal only, exactly like propose_gpu. Returns the command for the operator to approve. The agent must never start a batch.

Then the operator can say "look at D:\jobs\scene12 and tell me if it's ready" and get a real answer, followed by a command they run themselves.
Verify
Build a synthetic job folder with 3 prompts, 3 video refs, a sequential img0/, a single fixed img1/, and a two-file img2/. Then:

pairing is correct and reported before anything renders
the fixed slot repeats; the sequential slots advance
natural sort puts 2 before 10
tags are one-based and contiguous, and match the sockets actually wired
a render with only two images emits <Picture 1>/<Picture 2> and no <Picture 3>
the motion lock appears in all three places: subject definition, retention line with weak_reference, and detailed description
mismatched counts warn and show the pairing rather than truncating silently
an invalid prompt is skipped with its faults listed, not rendered
--limit 1 renders exactly one
re-running skips completed renders; --force redoes them
nothing under outputs/equal_shares/** is read or written — verify by timestamp
the queue owner is claimed and released
batch_render refuses to execute and returns a command instead
guard rails still refuse; validate_h3_prompt.py still 124/124 on the Equal Shares set
Do not stop
Work through. The one legitimate stop is Job 1 finding that no video reference socket exists — report that clearly and continue building everything else, with the motion reference disabled and the reason recorded.

Finish with a CHANGELOG/ entry: the real socket name you found, the tag mapping as implemented, and whether the validator needed adjusting for this prompt shape.
